name: Unakite
physical: Traditionally linked to a calm, balanced feeling
Associated with comfort during emotional stress
Often kept nearby for gentle support
summary: Unakite is the pink-and-green granite stone of balance and gentle emotional renewal, taking its name from the Unaka Mountains of the Appalachians.
intro: Unakite is a granite rock altered by hydrothermal fluids, giving it a speckled mix of pistachio-green epidote, salmon-pink orthoclase feldspar, and often clear to grey quartz. The result is a mossy-green stone shot through with pink blotches, and it polishes to a soft, satin shine. Because it is a rock, not a single mineral, every piece is a bit different. It is tough and inexpensive, and found as tumbled stones, spheres, palm stones and beads. The balance of green and pink makes it a natural fit for heart chakra work, something many crystal fans find immediately appealing.
history: Unakite takes its name from the Unaka Range, part of the Appalachian Mountains on the border of North Carolina and Tennessee, where it was first described in the nineteenth century. Virginia and North Carolina later became well-known sources, and the stone is a regional favorite among rockhounds in the eastern United States. Similar rocks are mined in South Africa, Brazil and China. Native American and early American craftspeople used local stones for beads and tools, though unakite in particular is mostly a modern lapidary favorite. Its combination of colors made it a staple of the 1970s crystal revival, and it remains a go-to heart stone.
meaning: Unakite is the stone of balance in the heart chakra tradition. Healers say the green brings growth and calm, and the pink brings compassion and gentle love, together helping people feel emotionally steady. It is used for working through old hurts, for being patient with oneself and for new starts after loss. Many practitioners link it to the concept of rebirth, because it is said to encourage looking back at the past and letting go. People also use it for balancing feelings between giving and receiving in relationships. Its energy is often described as soft but persistent, never forcing. It is a favorite for those starting emotional work or looking for a gentle companion.
howToUse: Wear unakite as a pendant or bracelet near the heart for gentle, ongoing balance. Hold a palm stone during quiet journaling or meditation, with one hand over the chest. Place a stone on a bedside table to encourage calm reflection at night. Carry one when you are working through a tender situation. Give a tumbled stone to someone who needs encouragement. Combine it with rose quartz for extra softness, or with clear quartz to clarify your thoughts.
care: Unakite is tough and tolerates water, so rinse it under lukewarm water and dry it with a soft cloth. Cleanse by smoke, sound, moonlight, burying in soil or resting on selenite. It handles sunlight, so charging in daylight is fine. Because it is a rock, avoid hard knocks and sudden temperature changes. Store it apart from harder gems and avoid harsh cleaners.
identify: Genuine unakite has a speckled mix of green epidote and pink feldspar with grey or clear quartz bits, never a perfect pattern. Dyed or painted stones show uniform color or surface-only pigment. Glass and resin fakes look too regular and feel lighter or warmer. Real stone is cool, dense and takes a fine polish. Cheap strands of pink-and-green beads may be dyed jasper, so check hole edges for color pooling.

faq.a: Unakite is used for emotional balance, gentle heart healing and patience. Crystal healers link it to the heart chakra and carry it when working through old hurts or beginning a fresh chapter.

Unakite is a granite rock containing pink orthoclase feldspar, green epidote and often quartz. The hydrothermal alteration of the granite produced its colors, so it is a rock rather than a single mineral.
It is named after the Unaka Range in the Appalachian Mountains of North Carolina and Tennessee, where it was first described. The stone is also commonly found in Virginia.
